paragraphs.text: We have already seen what Scripture declares about death and resurrection. The question left standing is simpler and harder: do we actually live as though it were true?
notes: Chapter opener. Backward pointer to prior resurrection teaching is authorized by editorial continuity and CH016 purpose.
The standing question restates section purpose (lived attitude), not a new argument.
Provider kind=con is not trusted automatically; human reading confirms non-substantive orientation.

paragraphs.text: Do not ever be afraid of death. There is no fixed hour appointed that fear can calculate or bargain with, and so fear itself is out of place. If somebody has gone to heaven, that should not produce dread in us. It should be our joy.
notes: Direct written transformation of IDEA224 and its SRC set.
No-set-time claim is in the IDEA summary; remaining clauses match SRC006149/183/187.

paragraphs.text: Yet we can see fear operating in believers, and this is not normal. Fear of death is an abuse — an abuse to your very person, a diminishment of what you were made and remade to be. It is worth naming where this abuse comes from. The devil has used it since the beginning; he has not changed his style. The same old strategy that first weaponized death against humanity is still being run today, unchanged, because it still works wherever it is not resisted by truth.
notes: Core IDEA225 is clearly present: abuse to the person, devil's unchanged old strategy.
QUESTIONABLE clause: 'because it still works wherever it is not resisted by truth' is a new causal implication absent from IDEA/SRC.
'first weaponized death against humanity' is stronger historical framing than 'has used it since' / 'old strategy'.
Not an invented example. Not empty. Not an unknown handle.

paragraphs.text: But this is not a matter of mental technique. It is not mind over matter, not a trick of positive thinking applied to a frightening subject. Death as gain must become your reality — not an idea you agree with in a sermon and set aside, but the actual substance of how you face your own ending.
notes: IDEA226 lived-reality vs intellectual idea. SRC006192 mind-over-matter preserved.
Positive-thinking / sermon phrasing is stylistic expansion, not a new doctrine.

paragraphs.text: And this is exactly where the trouble shows itself. Of recent, there has been word of the death of many supposed children of God who did not embrace death as gain. Whenever I hear that a child of God has gone and given account to God, my first question is: how were the last hours? Too often the answer that comes back is that he died saying, I don't want to die now, or she died saying the same. I am sincerely worried and troubled by this, because I do not know whether it means the church has not been filled enough with what it claims to believe.
notes: Near-direct written transformation of SRC007115-118.
Source-supported pastoral observation, not an invented example.
Automated lexical overlap under-scored IDEA250; human reading: CLEARLY_REPRESENTED.

paragraphs.text: The question underneath all of this is answered in Philippians chapter 1, verse 21: to live is Christ, and to die is gain. Christ is my life. To live is Christ — whatever that life might consist of, whatever it might mean to live, it is Christ. But if you do not practice Christ, death will be difficult for you. You have to practice Christ. If you are not practicing life now, death will be heavy when it comes, because what you have not lived you cannot suddenly possess at the threshold.
notes: REF051 is complete (Philippians chapter 1, verse 21). 'To die is gain' is the chapter theme and the complete-verse wording, not a new citation.
Practice-Christ / death-heavy clauses match SRC007155-162 and IDEA251.
Threshold clause is a restatement of not-practicing-life → death-heavy, not a new doctrine.

paragraphs.text: There is another side to this, and it is worth holding up as evidence that the reality is attainable, not theoretical. I know at least two men who foreknew the exact hour, the exact date, of their own death, and met it without distress — one of them telling those around him, so you better come, I'll go to heaven, as calmly as a man announcing a journey already planned and welcomed.
notes: Source-supported testimony example. Exact hour/date and quoted speech are in SRC007193-204.
Journey simile is stylistic dressing of sourced speech, not a new anecdote.
Historical funeral illustration did not recur.

paragraphs.text: This is the ground on which 1 Corinthians 15 stands — not as a chapter to be admired for its argument, but as a reality meant to be lived into, so that the sting long since removed from death is not merely a doctrine we recite but a gain we actually practice.
notes: 1 Corinthians 15 citation itself is REF050 / SRC006788 and is supported.
QUESTIONABLE: 'the sting long since removed from death' completes partial REF050 with 1 Cor 15:55-57 content not present in the supplied CH016 evidence.
Lived-vs-recited closer restates chapter purpose and is otherwise in bounds.
Not an invented named reference. Not an invented funeral example. Not an empty paragraph.
